still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month on the brand box, and almost nobody pays it.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, and Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the incretin labels.
The FDA has approved no generic tirzepatide; Zepbound and Mounjaro remain brand-only in the US, and no incretin implant is on the market.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 39.5% ever-used − 29.8% current = 9.7% used and are off now (≈26.6M adults). About half of current users are on a second or later course (14.9 points). That share is down from 55% because the 10.7-point rise in ever-use brought in mostly first-course users. Another 2.6 points cycled and are off again, so (14.9 + 2.6) / 39.5 ≈ 44% of ever-users have cycled. The other ~7.1 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence near one-third on weekly and oral products and restart rates of 36–47%, which cheap generics pushed toward the top of that range. Age check: 0.20×17 + 0.33×28.5 + 0.24×39 + 0.23×33 = 3.4 + 9.4 + 9.4 + 7.6 ≈ 29.8. Income thirds average 29.8, and the bottom third gained most (+12.5 points) through Medicaid, the HRSA programme and $45–69 generics. Users: 29.8% of ~274M adults ≈ 81.6M. FICTIONAL payer mix: Medicare 27% (~22.0M; ~20.8M are 65+, ≈33% of ~63M older adults), Medicaid 13% (~10.6M), HRSA free provision 6% (~4.9M), so public programmes pay for 46% (~37.5M). Commercial is 19% (~15.5M), legitimate cash 27% (~22.1M) and gray market 8% (~6.5M, down from 7.5M). Adult obesity has fallen to ~31.6%. About 15% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in Mississippi, rural Tennessee and among men 18–29. Pediatric: ~1.6% of under-18s are on a drug and ~3.6% of 12–17s, the rise driven by Medicaid EPSDT coverage of generic semaglutide for adolescents. Under-12 use is flat at ~0.25% of 6–11s. About 4.1M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping, and ~21M live with a parent currently on a drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~22.0M users). The Generic Metabolic Access Act (Dec 2033) added Part D coverage for chronic weight management from Jan 2034. The benefit is limited to generic or multisource incretins (generic semaglutide injection, generic liraglutide) for BMI ≥35, or ≥30 with a comorbidity, with reauthorisation at 12 months on ≥5% loss. Brand products are still reached only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA and dementia-risk codes, now behind generic-first step therapy. FICTIONAL arithmetic: brand 9.5M × ~$210 net × 12 ≈ $23.9B, plus generic 12.5M (8.0M new obesity-benefit users + 4.5M switched) × ~$36 × 12 ≈ $5.4B, gives ≈ $29.3B gross Part D incretin spend. That is below 2032's $31.6B even though users roughly doubled. Medicaid (~10.6M users): 31 states plus DC now cover weight-loss use, up from 7, drawn in by a 90% federal match on generic incretins for 2034–36. Mississippi and Tennessee declined. FICTIONAL arithmetic: brand 2.8M × ~$180 × 12 ≈ $6.0B, plus generic 7.8M × ~$25 × 12 ≈ $2.3B, ≈ $8.4B. HRSA Community Metabolic Access Program: free generic semaglutide through FQHCs and 340B clinics for uninsured and underinsured adults, ~4.9M enrollees. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 4.9M × ($18 contract drug + $10 dispensing) × 12 ≈ $1.65B, inside a $1.8B/year appropriation. CBO score of the Act: Medicare new benefit ~$3.5B/yr (8M × $36 × 12) + Medicaid federal increment ~$1.4B/yr + HRSA $1.8B/yr − ~$1.9B/yr step-therapy offsets ≈ $4.8B/yr, or ~$48B over ten years.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide sells for $4–30 a month abroad. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials are $20–60 in markets without enforceable patents, but Chinese export licensing on protected amino acids has tightened supply and pushed Indian API costs up ~15–20%. Canadian and Brazilian generics run CAD 40–70 and BRL 150–260. India and China still supply about 60% of world incretin volume, down from two-thirds.
access.note: FICTIONAL. US generic semaglutide injection launched in Mar 2033 after Novo settled its remaining patent suits. Four ANDA holders and a Novo authorised generic were on the market by late 2033. Cash prices for a monthly supply are $39–69 at warehouse clubs, Cost Plus-style pharmacies and telehealth. Tariffs set the floor: makers using Indian API pay 25% and Chinese inputs carry 50%, so US generics settled at roughly 3–10× Indian prices rather than at parity. The brands answered. Wegovy pill maintenance is $179 on TrumpRx (starting doses stay $149). Foundayo is $99–149. Zepbound is $229–279 cash. MariTide is $229 direct, still clinic-administered in employer tracks (~6.0M enrollees, ~4.4M on MariTide). Retatrutide is ~$379 direct. No oral generic exists, because the SNAC formulation patents still hold. Orals are now ~36% of users and generic weekly injections ~31%. Employer coverage rose to 37%, almost all of it through generic-first formularies. The gray market shrank to ~6.5M users and changed shape. Indian semaglutide vials lost most of their price advantage. Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide copies, which have no legal generic competitor, now make up most of it, sold through Telegram and WhatsApp resellers. Calm and focus subscriptions fell to ~1.1M, all inside the cash channel.

on_market_classes: GLP-1 agonist, weekly injectable (semaglutide: Wegovy/Ozempic; generic semaglutide injection since Mar 2033)
GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist/GIP-receptor antagonist antibody conjugate, monthly injectable (maridebart cafraglutide: MariTide)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: cardiovascular risk reduction (semaglutide incl. generics; tirzepatide)
pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics, with growth-monitoring labelling)
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide); the extension to adults without CVD is still not approved
mainstream_offlabel_uses: planned 'drug holidays' and self-directed dose reduction to manage flatness, now common practice and written into obesity-medicine guidance
'calm' and 'focus' microdosing through telehealth (~1.1M subscribers), plus DIY microdosing of cheap generic semaglutide vials
alcohol reduction via telehealth and employer EAPs after the AUD sNDA received a CRL
dementia-prevention use by 50–70-year-olds without CVD, now mostly cash generic semaglutide at $39–69 instead of tirzepatide
semaglutide in under-12s with severe obesity (off-label, low and flat)
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. No new class and no new indication reached the market in 2033–34. The one new product form is generic semaglutide injection (ANDA approvals Mar 2033 after Novo's settlement). It realises the generic_collapse price path and is not a new class. The oral semaglutide AUD sNDA (filed Jan 2032) received a CRL in Nov 2033: the FDA asked for a second adequate trial and dose-response data, and also cited the unresolved reward-blunting question. Bimagrumab-type lean-mass adjuncts (filed Jul 2032) received a CRL in Aug 2033 for lack of functional benefit; a resubmission with gait and fracture endpoints is planned for 2036. Lilly's tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial read out in Oct 2034 with a modest benefit, and resubmission is expected in 2035, so no approval came in this window. Implant programmes are in phase 2 and not on the market. No oral matches tirzepatide. Global incretin revenue was ~$158B in 2033, the first annual fall, as US semaglutide revenue moved to generics while global volume kept rising.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Generic switchers report a transient rise in nausea when pen-to-vial changes alter their titration schedules. Chronic diarrhoea in long-term users is routinely worked up for EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained on brand and generic labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Persistent gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction, including symptoms after discontinuation
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Cohorts show ~1.5–2× gastroparesis diagnoses on drug, but the excess persisting after discontinuation is inconsistent across studies. This is the second-largest claim category in the MDL.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus already in adverse reactions. No new warning. Litigation is the main venue, now at mass-tort scale (see EPI).

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss. Absolute cholecystectomy counts are rising with the Medicare expansion.
Still no causal confirmation of acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Plaintiffs plead it alongside EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; included in the consolidated MDL.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Hip-fracture HR holds at ~1.3 in users 65+ after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles. The ratio is unchanged, but the number of exposed older adults roughly doubled under the Part D generic benefit, which does not fund DXA or strength coaching. CMS claims show roughly a 9% rise in hip-fracture admissions among 65+ incretin users from 2033 to 2034.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained. The CRL on the bimagrumab adjunct left no approved muscle-preserving drug. CMS covers a DXA code but does not require it for Part D reauthorisation.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new adult signal in the far larger 2034 user base.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', 'the flats', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing observational study (published Sep 2033, n≈410,000) found clinically meaningful anhedonia in ~6.8% of users on maintenance doses vs ~3.1% of matched controls, ~9.6% on retatrutide and ~4.0% at calm-plan doses (not significant vs controls). Symptoms resolved in most within 6–10 weeks off drug. About a third of current users report at least one planned holiday or self-reduction a year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Apathy and anhedonia added to postmarketing adverse reactions on all incretin labels (May 2034); no boxed warning. Obesity Medicine Association guidance (Jun 2034) describes structured dose reduction and holidays, with weight and glucose monitoring.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. Long holidays of 4+ weeks on weekly products produce partial regain and re-titration GI symptoms.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins the chronic-therapy framing, the Part D 12-month reauthorisation and employer adherence verification.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency in low-intake users. Fat-soluble deficiency is tied to EPI. Most HRSA-programme users get no annual micronutrient panel.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual panel language carried onto generic semaglutide labels.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after 5+ years on semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Tirzepatide's excess is still small and non-significant. By Jun 2034 the consolidated GLP-1 MDL in the Eastern District of Pennsylvania held ~74,000 filed claims, mostly EPI and gastroparesis. In the first EPI bellwether (Jun 2034) a jury awarded $8.4M compensatory against Novo for pre-2031 failure to warn. Novo booked a $4.1B litigation reserve. Under PLIVA v. Mensing, users injured on generic semaglutide cannot sue generic makers for failure to warn, so the group most of the public-programme users will fall into has no tort remedy except innovator-liability claims in California and a few other states.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling retained. Tirzepatide review continues. Two Senate bills to restore generic-user failure-to-warn claims have not left committee.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in adolescents and children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling and of drug holidays
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. The effects of holiday cycling on bone, pancreas and immunogenicity are uncharacterised. The new Medicare cohort is the largest older-adult exposure ever studied.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; CMS-FDA Sentinel linkage expanded to Part D generic users.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Cumulative FDA adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~31,000. New cases concentrate in Chinese tirzepatide and retatrutide copies; there was no 2031-scale cluster in 2033–34. Poison-centre calls are ~4× 2025 levels, down from ~5×.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Tariff enforcement folded peptide parcels into CBP's de minimis crackdown. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.effect: Generic transition errors (concentration and device mismatches when switching from branded pens to generic pens or vials)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ISMP and poison centres report several thousand dosing-error calls since Mar 2033, mostly older Medicare switchers given multi-dose vials after years on fixed-dose pens. A few hundred ED visits for vomiting and dehydration.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA labelling and carton-design guidance for generic semaglutide (Feb 2034); some Part D plans now require pen presentations for 75+.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: At 36 months the liraglutide 6–11 PMR shows height velocity ~0.6 cm/year below expected in children who were prepubertal at start, with partial catch-up in those who stopped. The Swedish registry findings (later puberty in boys, ARFID HR ~1.8) were replicated in a Danish cohort. Final adult height is still unknown. Medicaid EPSDT adolescent use roughly doubled, and growth-chart compliance in Medicaid claims runs ~55%.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA labelling unchanged since Apr 2032, with no age restriction. EMA CHMP (2033) advised against starting prepubertal children except severe obesity with comorbidity. AAP lifestyle-first interim guidance stands.

food_and_beverage.state: About 45% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~14% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~12%, and dollar sales fell ~2% in 2034, the first real decline. The 2032 class split broke down as the bottom third medicated: Dollar General and Family Dollar value packs and private-label snacks lost volume fastest in the Delta and Appalachia in 2034. Kroger is re-planning lower-income stores toward small-format protein and frozen. Mondelez and Hershey announced US plant consolidations.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~17% from 2025 and beer ~11%. Losses spread from insured suburbs to working-class markets as Medicaid and HRSA users reached heavy drinkers. Independent bar closures continue in Midwestern mid-sized cities, and holiday-week drinking is visible: users report drinking more on off-weeks. Non-alcoholic drinks grow but remain small.

restaurants.state: Traffic is down ~2–3%. QSR value menus, the 2032 growth segment in lower-income markets, stalled as regainers restarted on cheap generics. Casual dining keeps portion tiers. Some chains now market 'off-week' indulgence promotions.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists are consolidating again. Mass retailers moved size runs down across most zip codes. Resale and stretch keep serving cyclers and holiday-takers whose weight swings a few kilograms.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. YMCA and some FQHCs run grant-funded 'Strong Start' sessions for HRSA-programme users, but capacity reaches under a tenth of enrollees. Premium DXA-plus-coaching memberships hold at $250–400.

insurance.state: Employer coverage rose to 37% on generic-first formularies. Pharmacy trend fell to ~+3% as brand semaglutide moved to generic. Part D 2035 national average bids came in flat despite the new benefit, because step therapy cut brand spend. Adherence-verified premium differentials persist and collide with holiday protocols: more employees appeal 'non-adherence' flags caused by clinician-recommended breaks.

pharma.state: Novo's US semaglutide revenue fell ~45% as it moved to generics and the authorised generic, and Novo leans on the Wegovy pill and CagriSema. Lilly holds the premium market with tirzepatide and retatrutide, which have no generic. Amgen's MariTide is stable in employer tracks. Cardinal Peptide Works, a DPA Title III-backed joint venture in Sanford, North Carolina, holds the HRSA contract at $18/month and ~12% of US generic semaglutide volume. Generic margins are thin and tariff-dependent. Litigation reserves now sit on Novo's balance sheet.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Weight no longer reads as income; the drug you are on does. The 'county shot' body, from free generic semaglutide at the FQHC, is thinner than in 2032 but soft and uncoached. Lean with muscle still means covered and coached, now with brand tirzepatide or MariTide. Among older adults, a cane after a fall is becoming a recognisable sign of a late, unscanned start on the Medicare benefit.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle is still the uniform in Charlotte and Austin, and 'brand' is a whispered distinction. On the Columbus corridor the plant-clinic MariTide body persists. In Memphis the visible change is the cycler's body steadying as people move from bad vials to the county shot. Across the state line in Mississippi, which declined the enhanced Medicaid match, the cycler is still the norm. The bottom third's weight gap with the top narrowed sharply, but its muscle and bone gap did not.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter. Drug holidays have created a new ritual calendar: people schedule off-weeks around weddings, Thanksgiving and church homecomings, and hosts ask 'are you on or off that week'. The Bread Alone fasting network claims ~1,100 congregations, many in the Mid-South, and preaches fasting as the alternative to 'the government's shot'. School-lunch debates now turn on whether districts should refer students to Medicaid incretin screening.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Lean-mass verified' badges persist. 'Off-week' is a dating-app status, and some couples align holidays. Therapists report that flatness complaints became speakable after the 2034 label change: 'it's on the label now'.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is now politically coded. The backlash, which in 2032 was split, found a shared target in public provision. The 'Whole Body' coalition puts fat-acceptance revivalists in Los Angeles and Portland on the same stages as MAHA activists and Bread Alone pastors, arguing that hunger is a person's own and that a federal shot for the poor is management, not care. They disagree on almost everything else.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: FDA observational data put clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~6.8% of maintenance-dose users vs ~3.1% of controls, ~9.6% on retatrutide and ~4.0% at calm-plan doses. Applied to ~81.6M users, the maintenance-dose excess alone implies roughly 2.5–3M people with a drug-attributable loss of pleasure. About a third of users take at least one planned holiday or dose reduction a year. Calm subscriptions fell from 1.3M to ~1.1M as the complaint went mainstream and DIY generic microdosing grew.
interior_life.framing: A side effect you manage. 'The flats' is the common name. Clinicians prescribe holidays; employers' adherence systems record them as missed doses; calm platforms rebranded from 'quiet the noise' to 'steady dosing with built-in breaks'. The backlash calls it sedation, and calls the subsidy sedation by appropriation.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 6.0M employees are in adherence-verified tracks. Clinician-ordered holidays now trigger premium-differential flags, and benefits vendors added a 'documented holiday' code that roughly half of mid-sized self-insured firms accept. The two EEOC ADA charges were joined by ~40 more on holiday-related penalties, all unresolved. Upper-tier staff talk about 'off-week sharpness' before quarterly reviews.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir became 'holiday' comedy: stand-up and sitcom plots built around the week everything comes back. Calm-segment streaming lost ground. Sportsbooks report wagering spikes among users in holiday weeks, and some now time promotions to the first of the month.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Couples schedule holidays together. Couples' practices report fewer desire-mismatch intakes than in 2032, as flatness got a shared name and a protocol, but more conflict over holiday timing and holiday drinking.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The flats became a political argument. Whole Body and MAHA-aligned legislators in Tennessee and Mississippi cited the 2034 label change when keeping their states out of the 90% match. Supporters of the Act frame the HRSA programme as heart-attack prevention. There is still no turnout evidence for a sedated electorate.

state.regulatory_posture: Permissive on approvals, active on payment. FDA approved generic semaglutide, issued CRLs on the AUD sNDA and the muscle adjunct, added anhedonia and apathy to labels, and issued generic carton guidance. Congress passed the Generic Metabolic Access Act. No state acted on adherence premiums; Illinois's ban is still the only one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Direct subsidy as public-health policy. Under the Dec 2033 Act: Part D obesity coverage for generics from Jan 2034, a 90% federal Medicaid match for generic incretins in 2034–36 (31 states plus DC opted in), and the $1.8B/year HRSA Community Metabolic Access Program providing free generic semaglutide through FQHCs to ~4.9M people. No mandate. The 2027 tri-agency 30% wellness guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Part D reauthorisation requires a documented ≥5% loss at 12 months. HRSA enrollment requires quarterly clinic weigh-ins logged to a federal registry for programme evaluation. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress. Employer wellness vendors still receive clinic and PBM records under consent, and calm platforms still sell de-identified cohorts.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE added generic semaglutide for weight management for beneficiaries in Oct 2034. The Army recruit oral pilot continues. DOT still has not ruled on incretin, calm-plan or holiday use among commercial drivers.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Section 232 tariffs (Jun 2033) put 50% duties on Chinese and 25% on Indian peptide APIs and finished incretins, with exemptions for US-content producers. In Aug 2033 China imposed export licensing on Fmoc-protected amino acids and synthesis resins. Cardinal Peptide Works was named a DPA Title III national-champion supplier with a $1.2B federal loan. US–India talks stalled over the tariffs. The US cash-to-Indian-generic gap fell from ~40–50× to ~3–10×.

events.event: FDA approves the first generic semaglutide injections from four ANDA holders after Novo Nordisk settles its remaining US patent suits; Novo launches an authorised generic and cash prices fall to $39–69 a month by December

Commerce imposes Section 232 tariffs of 50% on Chinese and 25% on Indian peptide ingredients and finished weight-loss drugs; Beijing answers in August with export licensing on key peptide building blocks, and Cardinal Peptide Works in North Carolina wins a $1.2B Defense Production Act loan

Congress passes the Generic Metabolic Access Act in a year-end package, adding Medicare Part D coverage for generic weight-loss drugs from January, a 90% federal Medicaid match and $1.8B a year for free provision at community health centres; CBO scores it at ~$48B over ten years

FDA adds apathy and anhedonia to the adverse-reactions section of every incretin label after its observational study finds dose-related emotional flattening; within weeks the Obesity Medicine Association publishes guidance on structured dose reductions and drug holidays

In the first pancreatic bellwether of the consolidated GLP-1 litigation, now ~74,000 claims, a Philadelphia federal jury awards $8.4M against Novo Nordisk; generic users remain barred from suing generic makers under PLIVA v. Mensing
The 'Whole Body' coalition draws ~40,000 people to Nashville's Legislative Plaza against 'the government shot'; Tennessee and Mississippi confirm they will stay out of the enhanced Medicaid match

open_tensions: Most public-programme users are on generic semaglutide, and under PLIVA v. Mensing those injured by it cannot sue its makers for failure to warn. Tort liability for the pancreatic harms of a federally subsidised drug falls on Novo for past brand use and on nobody for future generic use, and Congress has not moved.

The Part D generic benefit roughly doubled the number of older adults exposed to a drug with a hip-fracture HR of ~1.3, without funding DXA, strength coaching or a muscle adjunct, which the FDA declined. Fracture admissions are rising while the spending line looks like a success.

The $39–69 generic floor rests on tariffs, a single national-champion contractor and Chinese export licences. Any of them could move the price. Meanwhile the gray market has shifted to tirzepatide and retatrutide copies that no legal generic undercuts.

Clinicians now prescribe drug holidays, while employer adherence systems and Part D reauthorisation punish gaps. In Mississippi and Tennessee the backlash kept the bottom third on vials and the county shot, outside the Medicaid expansion.

prose.headline: The County Shot: $49 Semaglutide, a Federal Pharmacy for 37 Million, and a Country Learning to Take Weeks Off
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 three American adults in ten take an incretin drug, about eighty-two million people, and four in ten have tried one. The jump of ten points in two years did not come from a new molecule. It came from the expiry of an old one. In March 2033 Novo Nordisk settled its last patent suits, the FDA approved generic semaglutide injections, and by Christmas a month's supply cost $49 at a warehouse club. Wegovy's list price is still printed as $1,349, and the starting pill is still $149 on the government's cash site. Those numbers now describe the expensive end of the market, not the market.

Cheap made it politically possible to pay. In December 2033 Congress folded the Generic Metabolic Access Act into a year-end package. Medicare now covers weight-loss treatment, but only with generics. States that add coverage get a ninety percent federal match, and community health centres hand out free semaglutide to the uninsured. CBO scored the whole thing at under five billion dollars a year. Medicare's incretin bill fell slightly even as its users roughly doubled, because plans now make patients try generics before brands. Public programmes pay for nearly half of all users. The bottom third of earners, once the least medicated, gained more than twelve points.

The price has a floor, and the floor is political. In June 2033 Washington put tariffs on Chinese and Indian peptide ingredients. Beijing answered with export licences on the chemical building blocks Indian factories also buy. A Defense Production Act loan made Cardinal Peptide Works in Sanford, North Carolina, the contract supplier for the free programme at $18 a month. American generics settled at several times Indian prices rather than near them. The gray market shrank, but it did not disappear. It moved to copies of tirzepatide and retatrutide, which have no legal generic and still cost two hundred dollars and up.

The lawsuits caught up with the old drug just as the new payers arrived. About seventy-four thousand claims sit in a Philadelphia federal court, most alleging pancreatic insufficiency or a stomach that never woke up. In June a jury awarded a woman $8.4 million against Novo for warnings that came too late. Under a 2011 Supreme Court ruling, people injured by a generic cannot sue its maker for failure to warn. Most of the people on the county shot will be in that position.

The flatness has a name now, and a label line. In May the FDA added apathy and anhedonia to every incretin label after its own study found dose-related losses of pleasure in about one heavy user in fifteen. Doctors began prescribing holidays. People skip a week before a wedding, a funeral or Thanksgiving, and hosts ask whether a guest is on or off. Employer adherence systems record those weeks as failures, and the complaints at the EEOC have multiplied. The calm subscriptions shrank. It is easier to buy a vial and dose down yourself.

The backlash also found a shared target. In September forty thousand people filled Legislative Plaza in Nashville under the Whole Body banner: fat-acceptance organisers, MAHA activists and pastors from the Bread Alone fasting network, which now claims eleven hundred congregations. They disagreed about bodies and agreed that a federal shot for the poor is management dressed as care. Tennessee and Mississippi stayed out of the Medicaid expansion. Across the line in Mississippi, the cycler is still the common body.

In most places the bodies are thinner and softer. The weight gap between rich and poor narrowed. The muscle gap did not. Older adults started late through Medicare, often without a bone scan, and hip-fracture admissions are climbing in that group while the budget line reads as a success. Nobody knows yet how tall the children will grow. From a distance it looks like the most successful public-health programme in a generation, and in several respects it is.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Darlene Pruitt does not take her shot on Thursday. The pen sits in the butter compartment with the Part D sticker still on the box: generic semaglutide, $4.15 copay. Her grandson Marcus gets married Saturday in Whitehaven, and she means to taste the cake.

She drives her daughter Keisha to the clinic on Elvis Presley Boulevard for her quarterly weigh-in. Keisha's shot is free. The nurse types the number into a tablet and says Keisha's down nine percent. In the parking lot a man in a Whole Body T-shirt hands out flyers about the government shot. Keisha folds hers into a fan.

At Greater Bethel the fasting circle meets at noon. Pastor Ames says hunger is a teacher. Darlene sits in back because she hasn't fasted since March. She likes the singing and has missed it.

Her nephew Dre calls from Southaven to ask whether she can pick up a package at her address. It's the Chinese tirzepatide, ninety dollars. Mississippi won't cover his kind. She says not this time, baby, then says all right.

In the afternoon she reads about the Philadelphia verdict on her phone. Her sister was on the brand for six years. She saves the article.

By evening the cornbread smells like it used to. She eats two pieces standing at the counter and laughs at a commercial, really laughs, and stops to notice it.

She takes the stairs one at a time, a hand on the rail. The doctor never sent her for the bone scan. Saturday she will dance anyway, carefully.
